stories.headline: Update: S&P Global expects RBI to raise rates by 0.25% in December
stories.summary: In its Asia-Pacific outlook, S&P Global says it expects the RBI to lift its policy rate by another 25 basis points in December, and that the chance of one more hike in early 2027 has gone up. New since Monday's report of its 7% growth forecast for this year and next; it still sees inflation averaging 5.3% this year with risks tilted higher.
stories.why_it_matters: A December hike would raise borrowing costs for home, car and business loans and weigh on rate-sensitive stocks.
stories.note: Single source: All India Radio, reporting S&P Global's Asia-Pacific Q1 2027 outlook.

impact.why: An expected December RBI hike points to higher Indian bond yields and loan rates.
Higher rates lift lending margins but can slow loan demand.

stories.headline: India gives over 1 crore HPV vaccine doses to 14-year-old girls; WHO congratulates
stories.summary: India has given more than 10 million HPV vaccine doses to 14-year-old girls, about 87% of the yearly group eligible, to prevent cervical cancer. The WHO praised the effort, and PM Modi called it a big step in preventive healthcare.

stories.headline: Australia to fine tech giants up to 5% of global revenue for online harm
stories.summary: Australia's government says a new 'digital duty of care' law, agreed with the Greens and expected to pass Parliament this week, will let it fine platforms such as Google and Meta up to 5% of worldwide revenue, up from a planned A$109 million cap. People could also sue platforms and switch off algorithm feeds. Tech firms back the aim but say officials get too much say over what counts as harmful.
stories.note: Single source: Al Jazeera (with Reuters photo).

image.alt: Australian Communications Minister Anika Wells speaking at a news conference in Canberra

stories.headline: Iran's Ghalibaf says no talks with US until it meets Tehran's seven conditions
stories.summary: Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf says Tehran will not hold talks or take any step until Washington carries out Iran's seven conditions, and warned of a 'decisive response' if its enemies miscalculate. Earlier reports list demands such as lifting the US naval blockade, unfreezing Iranian funds and ending sanctions. The US has not responded.
stories.why_it_matters: A harder Iranian line keeps the Hormuz blockade and the oil supply risk in place for longer.
stories.note: Statement by Iran; repeats conditions first set out in September.

impact.why: No talks means the Hormuz blockade risk stays priced into oil.

stories.headline: UN chief Guterres asks countries to agree AI safety rules within a year
stories.summary: Speaking at an AI safety summit in Barbados on Monday, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres urged member states to build a global AI risk framework within the next year, with shared safety measures, testing and independent oversight. He said the UN, world finance and trade bodies still reflect the world of 1945 and need reform.

stories.headline: Rupee market shut for Gurpurab; dealers see 92.50 to 93.55 range when it reopens
stories.summary: Indian currency trading is closed today. The rupee last ended Monday near 92.9 per dollar after corporate dollar buying snapped a five-day rally (PTI put the close at 92.92, Business Standard at 92.91). Dealers quoted by Business Standard expect a 92.50 to 93.55 range, driven by fund flows. The dollar index was flat near 104.3 in Asia and Europe, and the yen weakened to about 159.4 per dollar.
stories.why_it_matters: A firm dollar before Wednesday's US inflation data limits room for the rupee to gain when trade resumes.
stories.note: Close differs by 1 paisa between PTI (92.92) and Business Standard (92.91).

impact.why: Range-bound: fund flows and the dollar decide the next move.

stories.headline: Update: Taiwan closes 9% higher, Kospi 6.3%, Nikkei 3.9% on Nvidia rebound
stories.summary: At the close, Taiwan's index jumped 9.0% to 40,122, South Korea's Kospi rose 6.3% to 5,006 and Japan's Nikkei 225 gained 3.9% to 58,645, after Nvidia rehired Jensen Huang as CEO. TSMC, Foxconn and MediaTek ended near Taiwan's 10% daily limit. Hong Kong's Hang Seng bucked the trend, slipping 0.8%. US stock futures were up about 0.1%. Indian markets are shut today and reopen on Wednesday.
stories.why_it_matters: A strong Asian rebound after Monday's 1.75% Nifty fall sets up a firmer start for Indian tech and broader stocks on Wednesday.
stories.note: Index closes from exchange data on Yahoo Finance; stock moves from CNBC.

image.alt: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang smiling and waving outdoors

impact.why: A big Asian rally points to a firmer Nifty open on Wednesday.
The tech-led rebound helps Indian IT and electronics names.

stories.headline: Brent holds near three-month low at about $89; gold slips 0.75%
stories.summary: Brent crude for January eased about 0.5% to near $89 a barrel and WTI to about $79.8, staying near their lowest since late August as Middle East supply recovers and inventories grow, despite Iran's mine claims. Gold futures fell about 0.75% to $3,624 an ounce and silver about 2% to $42.2. Correction: this morning's Brent figure of $86.3 was a later-dated contract.
stories.why_it_matters: Cheaper oil eases India's import bill and supports the rupee.

impact.why: Recovering supply and rising stocks keep Brent near a three-month low.
Lower oil cuts India's dollar demand for imports.
A firm dollar and Fed hike bets weigh on gold.

stories.headline: Google DeepMind AI agents make quantum algorithms up to 11.8x cheaper
stories.summary: Google DeepMind and Google Quantum AI say teams of Gemini 4 agents improved known quantum algorithms and proved each result correct in the Lean theorem prover. A fusion simulation became 11.8 times cheaper to run and needed 4,338 instead of 5,650 error-corrected qubits; a drug-metabolism enzyme simulation improved 2.5 times. The code and proofs are open-sourced.

stories.headline: OpenAI and Cisco release Shirudo, open-source tool to shield Linux servers before patches
stories.summary: OpenAI and Cisco launched Shirudo, an open-source runtime that uses Linux eBPF to put temporary 'shields' on running systems, blocking the code paths an exploit needs without a restart while patches are prepared. Security teams approve each shield. In a test, a Codex-made shield stopped a Java4Shell attack on a live Elasticsearch service.
